notes.claim: The lathe job: a 12.5 kW three-phase motor, power factor 0.91, efficiency 94%, in 90 degrees C thermosetting singles in trunking, with two other circuits, at 25 degrees C, behind a distribution circuit that drops 3%; the board voltage for Ib is therefore 388 V, and Ib = P / (sqrt3 x U x efficiency x pf) = 21.74 A (the mock prints 21.7 A).

Reference Method B (Table 4A2); Ca 1.02 at 25 degrees C for 90 degrees C thermosetting, Cg 0.70 for three circuits, It = In / (Ca x Cg) = 35.01 A, so 4 mm2 (37 A) from Table 4E1A column 5 where 2.5 mm2 (28 A) is too small; the terminals are assumed to allow 90 degrees C (the Table 4E1A note says the cable is rated at the lower of the cable's and the equipment's temperature).

Drop: 4 mm2 three-phase is 10 mV/A/m (Table 4E1B), 10 x 21.74 x 27 / 1000 = 5.87 V on the circuit, added to the 12 V upstream gives 17.87 V against the 20 V limit (the mock prints 17.859 V). For conductors of 16 mm2 or less the table gives one value and the lesson uses it as it stands; the rule 'tabulated value x cos phi' for 16 mm2 or less was not found in any quotable source, so the lesson does not teach it (the tabulated r and x split matters above 16 mm2).

Table 54.7 selection: same material as the line conductor and a line conductor of 16 mm2 or less gives a cpc of the line conductor's size, here 4 mm2. It is selection as an alternative to calculation, gives a larger csa than calculation, and a non-standard result needs the next size up; selection must not be used where the line conductors are sized only by short-circuit current or where earth fault current is less than short-circuit current (543.1.1).

A smaller cpc: with the board's Zdb 0.4 ohm (mock part 2; part 1's 0.97 ohm leaves no 25 A type C breaker able to pass), a 2.5 mm2 cpc with the 4 mm2 line gives R1+R2 12.02 mohm/m (On-Site Guide Table I1), x 1.28 x 27 m / 1000 = 0.415 ohm, Zs 0.815 ohm within the 25 A type C's 0.87 ohm; Ia is 250 A (Fig 3A5, 10 x In); the cpc carries Cmax current 310.43 A and the adiabatic S = sqrt(I2 t) / k with k 143 (Table 54.3) gives 0.69 mm2, under 2.5 mm2.

R1+R2 per metre for a 4 mm2 line with a 1.5 mm2 cpc is 16.71 mohm/m and with a 4 mm2 cpc 9.22 mohm/m (Table I1, corrected from the page image), so a 1.5 mm2 cpc at 27 m gives Zs 0.977 ohm, over 0.87 ohm.

Table 54.7 for a cpc of a different material from the line conductor is (k1 / k2) x S for a line conductor up to 16 mm2 and (k1 / k2) x 16 for over 16 up to 35 mm2, k1 for the line conductor and k2 for the protective conductor, each for its own material and insulation; his group handout works 143 x 6 / 46 = 18.65 mm2 and 143 x 16 / 46 = 49.73 mm2 (cut short from 49.74) with k2 = 46 for steel armour. The Goldberg Kabel page is a Singapore (SS 638) adoption of the same table, so the formula is corroborated, not the regulation number.

Armour as the cpc: its csa must be at least that found by calculation or by selection; it is thermally stressed in an earth fault and its end-to-end impedance (with glands and terminations) adds to Zs. A 6 mm2 four-core SWA has 36 mm2 of armour (needs 18.65 mm2), a 25 mm2 four-core has 70 mm2 (Prysmian, armour 2.3 ohm/km) and a 25 mm2 five-core 88 mm2 (1.8 ohm/km) against the 49.74 mm2 Table 54.7 needs.

When armour falls short: use a cable with an extra core, or run a separate cpc alongside; a separate cpc in parallel with an SWA cable is permitted (Regulation 521.5.1, as one practitioner's guide states) and must be sized for the full earth fault current, since the current does not share equally. With a core and the armour both as the cpc, R2 is the two in parallel, 1 / (1/0.727 + 1/1.8) = 0.518 mohm/m, and each path alone must also carry the fault current for the heat check, as his handout does.

The 40 A BS 88-2 fuse in the SWA example is taken to clear within 0.1 s at about 2.5 kA: not sourced for the 40 A rating. A maker's gate table shows an 80 A gG fuse operating within 0.1 s by 1100 A, and a 40 A fuse is the smaller fuse, so 2.5 kA is well past it; the lesson uses 0.1 s as a labelled practice value (case.json p.swa.t) and tells Dan to read the real time from Fig 3A3 in his copy.

Changed numbers: 70 degrees C thermoplastic at 35 degrees C has Ca 0.94 (Table 4B1); Cg 0.70 for three circuits; Table 4D1A column 5 gives 10 mm2 50 A and 16 mm2 68 A; Table 4D1B three-phase 16 mm2 is 2.4 mV/A/m. For the board, the upstream device's rated current must not exceed the board's rated current InA (Regulation 536.4.202, A4 wording as the Hager guide explains it), and InA is at least the sum of the design currents loaded together (IET Wiring Matters).

The Section A shapes of the C&G papers (design a final circuit end to end behind a distribution circuit, then the minimum suitable cpc considering design Zs and thermal constraints under fault conditions) are used as shapes only; every figure is Dan's mock's or changed.
